title: Uniboost cutover leaves a mid-flight mint-revert window on the swapped index: between replaceDispatcher and setPrice the new USDC-6dp dispatcher is live with the retired burner's 18-dp price
description: On a non-atomic mainnet Ledger broadcast (--slow --skip-simulation, three separate txs per index), _swapBurner lands replaceDispatcher(idx, uniboost) before setPrice(idx, 10e6). In that inter-tx window configs[idx] points at the USDC-6dp Uniboost dispatcher while still carrying the OLD burner's 18-dp target-token price (464.279e18 / 1.737e18 / 22876.13e18) and growth 1000. Read as raw 6-dp USDC, that price makes any mint on the affected index require an astronomically-unaffordable transferFrom, so the mint reverts. _trackConfig (line 435) checkpoints only after all three txs plus post-asserts succeed, so a resume idempotently re-runs the whole block (the second replaceDispatcher is a no-op because dispatcherToIndex[uniboost]==index).
impact: Transient, single-index mint-DoS with ZERO asset impact and a fail-safe (deny) direction: the mid-flight state can only make a mint revert on an unaffordable charge, never under-charge, mis-mint, or leak value. Under --slow the window is seconds-to-minutes; the harmful state persists only if the Ledger broadcast aborts (reject / gas spike / RPC failure) precisely between the replaceDispatcher tx and the setPrice tx, in which case that one index stays mint-reverting until the operator re-runs. Resume HEALS it because the checkpoint sits after all three mutations. No protocol-wide availability loss and no value leak keep it well below the Medium bar. A competent, non-malicious operator would be surprised that a partial broadcast leaves the index mint-reverting rather than cleanly disabled (Law-3 footgun test passes).
attackPath: Operator broadcasts the cutover on a Ledger with --slow --skip-simulation (three separate txs per index).
replaceDispatcher(idx, uniboost) lands: configs[idx] now points at the USDC-6dp Uniboost dispatcher but still carries the OLD burner's 18-dp price and growth 1000.
A user attempts a mint on idx before setPrice(idx, 10e6) lands -> NFTMinterV2._executeMint requires ~4.6e14..2.3e16 raw USDC -> reverts (fail-safe).
Happy path: setPrice + setGrowthFactor land seconds later, the window closes, _trackConfig checkpoints.
Abort path: the broadcast dies between the replace tx and the setPrice tx -> the index persistently mint-reverts until the operator re-runs to completion (resume heals).
recommendation: Eliminate the inter-tx window: disable the affected index around the reprice, or bundle replaceDispatcher + setPrice + setGrowthFactor into a single multicall so the new USDC-6dp dispatcher is never live with the retired burner's 18-dp price. This ensures a partial broadcast leaves the index cleanly disabled rather than silently mint-reverting.
